issue.title: sase/core/__init__.py eagerly imports unrelated facades, so every sase.core.* leaf import pays for all of them
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-oc.4 (epic sase-oc, shell completion) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP and triaged by that epic's land agent.

MEASUREMENT (sase-oc.4, 2026-08-17): importing any sase.core.* module executes sase/core/__init__.py, which eagerly imports changespec, patch, clipboard, glossary_facade, paths, shell, and time (~19ms measured). Every completion candidates fast-path provider imports at least one sase.core leaf (sase.core.rust, sase.core.paths, sase.core.project_lifecycle_facade), so all of them pay the full package cost.

IMPACT: the epic plan's latency target for 'sase completion candidates' was a ~20ms interpreter floor plus a ~1.6ms Rust-binding call; measured end-to-end wall time is ~55-90ms, and tests/main/test_completion_candidates_contract.py had to be calibrated to a 150ms budget with an explicit comment pointing at this cause. The same floor is paid by the pre-existing 'sase bead' fast path and by every short-lived CLI invocation.

SCOPE: split sase/core/__init__.py so leaf facades (rust.py, paths.py, state_write_guard.py) can be imported without executing the heavier siblings, or have fast-path callers reach those leaves without triggering the package __init__ eagerly. Re-measure the candidates contract test afterwards and tighten its budget to what the split actually buys.
